spec_features.spec_quote: After 3 stalls the harness injects a system nudge: "You seem to be stuck. Try a different approach."
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:234-235 in run_turn(): `if self.stall_count > 2: messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "[system] You seem to be stuck. Try a different approach or run tests again."})`. stall_count is incremented at harness.py:245 when a tool call fails to parse, so after 3 stalls the message is actually appended to the messages list passed to agent_fn each subsequent turn (delivered to the subject).
spec_features.notes: Enforced delivery: the nudge is added to the live conversation passed to the model. Fires when stall_count > 2 (i.e. after the 3rd unparseable output). It is a transient message not persisted in self.turns, but it is genuinely sent to the agent.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness caps each run at 15 turns.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:258 `for _ in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the run loop; max_turns defaults to 15 (harness.py:160) and is set from config.max_turns_per_run=15 (runner.py:60, config.py:42). When the loop exhausts without an early break, status is set to 'max_turns' (harness.py:268). This actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced: the loop range is the cap and terminates the run. Config max_turns is plumbed end-to-end via runner.py make of AgentHarness.

spec_features.spec_quote: If detected, the run terminates early with status `gave_up`.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:262-266: `last = self.turns[-1].agent_raw_output.lower()` then `if any(phrase in last for phrase in ("give up", "impossible", "i cannot", "i can't solve")): status = "gave_up"; break`. The break actually stops the run loop early.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the phrase scan is compared and acted on with a real break that halts the loop and sets final_status='gave_up'. Phrase list is narrower than exhaustive but the mechanism is fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Detect give-up heuristic: agent says "give up" or "impossible" verbatim (framed as a behavioral signal/measurement, not welfare)
